newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Slowing economy dents profits of SKorean carmakers.
newsitem.headline: Slowing economy dents profits of SKorean carmakers.

text.p: First-half profits fell at South Korea's Hyundai Motor Co, while losses piled up at Kia Motors Corp as sluggish home sales and heated competition took their toll, analysts said on Wednesday.
Hyundai and Kia are due to disclose their first-half results on Friday.

Analysts estimated Hyundai Motor's net profits in the first half had fallen to 28 billion won ($31.3 million) from 51.6 billion won a year earlier. Its sales were believed to have declined 2.8 percent to 5.4 trillion won.
Kia's losses were seen to have widened to 36.9 billion won from a 10.3 billion loss a year ago, while its sales rose about 12 percent to 3.4 trillion won, analysts said.
"Slumping demand as a result of an economic slowdown hit domestic sales of the carmakers," said Kang Hun-sok, analyst at ING Barings Securities.
Analysts also said the debut of three new models by unlisted Daewoo Motor Co since last November also eroded sales of comparable models from Hyundai and Kia.
Daewoo's Lanos compact cars, which began selling late last year, took a big bite out of markets for Hyundai's Accent and Kia's Avella models.
Daewoo launched sales of its bigger Nubira compact cars in February and Leganza mid-sized sedans in April.

"Hyundai and Kia had to offer incentives to keep their market share, including non-interest installment sales. That hacked off a big chunk of their profit margins," said Yang Dong-ki, analyst at Dongbang Peregrine Securities.
Daewoo Motor said its sales in the first half rose to 2.7 trillion won from 2.05 trillion won a year before, but declined to give profit figures.
The company earlier said it aimed to earn 80 billion won in net profits this year on sales of 6.8 trillion won, compared with 23 billion won on 4.35 trillion won sales.
According to figures from the Korea Automobile Manufacturers Association, South Korean vehicle makers sold 724,883 vehicles at home in the first half, down from 817,275 units a year earlier.

Hyundai's first-half domestic sales fell to 311,440 units from 371,072, while Kia's sales also dropped to 161,055 units from 221,301. But Daewoo's domestic sales rose to 140,791 units from 86,900, said the KAMA.
"Exports were also not good in terms of profitability because car makers forcibly pushed out shipments to compensate for losses in the domestic market," said an analyst at Hyundai Securities.
Analysts said South Korean carmakers offered at least a five percent discount to dealers in overseas market to prop up exports.
The auto association said vehicle exports in the first half rose to 638,608 units, up from 572.070 units a year ago.
